info.syllabusName: Japanese Culture & Japanese Studies_Đất nước và văn hóa Nhật Bản
info.timeAllocation:
Study Time (150h)
Including 45h in class (60 sessions) + 1.5h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description:
The course is divided into 2 main content areas:

1. Japan: This part mainly focuses on 3 topics: natural geography, history, and political system of Japan. The course content is summarized by the instructor into lecture slides from various sources and reference materials, without using a main textbook.
2. Japanese Culture: The course uses a main textbook, which contains 99 important keywords about Japanese culture, divided into 3 parts as follows:
・Part 1: Traditional Culture – familiar daily elements elevated into art forms (Chapter 1: Arts and Performance; Chapter 9: Festivals, Holidays, Religion; Chapter 5: Customs, Traditions, Ceremonies, etc.)
・Part 2: Everyday Life Culture – elements closely tied to Japanese daily life such as tatami mats, mixed rice, sushi rice balls, etc. (Chapter 3: Cuisine; Chapter 4: Housing, Architecture, Clothing; Chapter 7: Leisure, Entertainment, Music, Sports; Chapter 8: Literature, Thought, Spirit, etc.)
・Part 3: Studying Abroad in Japan – in relation to Japanese society and people.

In the Japanese Culture section, students read the main textbook, choose keywords of interest to explore in greater depth, report their findings, and present a deeper understanding of one or several keywords in their area of interest (students form groups of 2–3, prepare slides, and present in class).
Alternatively, students can register to carry out creative/experiential activities on a chosen theme, such as traditional food, tea ceremony, ikebana (flower arrangement), etc., and perform/demonstrate in class. Interactive activities with the audience are encouraged.

Thus, from these two areas, the specific objectives of the course are:
(1) Provide basic, general knowledge about Japan and Japanese culture such as geography, history, social system, traditional culture, arts, cuisine, clothing, architecture, etc., helping students understand distinctive features that shape Japan’s image in the world and in Vietnam.
(2) Provide basic vocabulary, some terminology, and expressions related to Japan and Japanese culture, helping reinforce and enhance language knowledge.
(3) Help students develop group work skills, independent research practice, and expand their knowledge by exploring a topic of personal/group interest.
(4) Enable students to report research results or conduct experiential activities to practice presentation skills and apply acquired knowledge in practice.
info.studentTasks:
・Attend at least 80% of in-class hours to qualify for the final exam.
・Read the textbook and present their understanding of assigned contents (in Japanese) in groups.
・Practice research by exploring issues related to Japanese culture, society, and people (with possible comparisons to Vietnam).
・Review lecture content, compare with instructor-provided materials and slides to firmly grasp knowledge and vocabulary related to Japanese culture and society.
・Actively participate in class discussions on given topics.
・Students may use AI (ChatGPT, Copilot, etc.) to improve learning effectiveness. AI can be applied specifically in the following areas:
1. Vocabulary: use AI to look up meanings of Japanese words and how they are used in context.
2. Knowledge of culture, society, and history: use AI to research information and terminology in reading passages related to the course topics, as well as in preparing presentations.
3. Review for Small Tests and Final Exam: use AI to systematically review learned content in a clear and scientific way.
info.tools:
・Lecture slides: used by the instructor to teach and shared with students.
・Main textbook: Japanese Culture – Essential Things to Know; students use the main textbook to read and expand on related course content.
・PPT: used by students for presentations.
・Japanese materials, tools, and costumes, etc., used to support presentations.

clos.loDetails: Recognize general knowledge about the natural conditions, climate, and administrative units of Japan.
Recognize basic knowledge about Japanese history and the characteristics of politics and culture in each historical period.
Recognize knowledge about Japan’s political system and the economic situation of Japan from after World War II to the present.
Recognize the cultural characteristics of Japan through annual festivals, traditional cultural forms, and clothing culture.
Understand basic knowledge and legal regulations related to studying abroad in Japan.
Practice group work skills and presentation skills about Japan and its people.
